documents.title: AI and Honor Code Advice for Faculty
documents.summary: Honor-system advice for faculty: instructors decide what resources are allowed, there is no one-size-fits-all university AI policy, and AI should be treated as unauthorized unless the instructor explicitly allows it. It tells instructors to put expectations in the syllabus, report unauthorized use to the Honor Council, and warn students that AI output is unreliable.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'the individual instructor determines what resources are permitted' and 'The university does not have a one-size-fits-all AI policy', which points to delegation. But it also tells faculty to say that, absent explicit authorization, students 'should consider AI to be an unauthorized resource', so AI is banned unless permitted. I code the default it sets (restrict) rather than delegates, because the document itself fixes the fallback.

units.why: The page opens by framing why guidance is needed: 'AI is a fast-evolving resource that has the potential to create confusion among students.' This is a purpose statement for the guidance, so it is a general principle (P56) that informs rather than directs.

documents.summary: Final report of the Provost's AI Policy Initiative: campus themes, a vision of human-centered augmented intelligence, and phased recommendations on Honor Code guidance, syllabus statements, research use, data security, training, a governing AI council, AI literacy, operations and copyright.
